2607.26397.title: Knowledge before Reasoning: EC-Reason-Bench, a Training-Free Diagnostic Benchmark for LLM Enzyme Classification
2607.26397.paper_summary: Enzyme function prediction is a hierarchical, knowledge-intensive form of protein function classification. Existing benchmarks expose an anomaly: general LLMs often get the coarse first level right, yet once asked for a complete EC number their accuracy at levels two through four drops to almost zero, while specialized models and tools stay usable. We propose EC-Reason-Bench, a training-free, diagnostic evaluation protocol built to answer two questions: why general LLMs score close to nothing on EC number prediction, and how much of that loss can be recovered without updating a single weight. We break enzyme classification ability into four orthogonal levers that can each be measured on their own: output structure, external knowledge, reasoning structure, and reasoning robustness. We test each lever with an inference-time method against a shared zero-shot baseline reproducing previously reported near-zero performance. Experiments with several strong reasoning LLMs yield four main findings. First, external knowledge is decisive and must precede reasoning: uniformly low closed-book performance rises sharply with open-book access, narrowing model gaps. Second, in closed-book settings, whether cascading and chain-of-thought help or hurt depends on a model's tendency to abstain. Third, once evidence is available the aggregate score of the best LLM setting is indistinguishable from simply voting the EC numbers of the nearest retrieved neighbors; that tie is an artifact of averaging, and it hides a large gain on adversarial evidence set against an equally large loss on multi-functional enzymes. Reasoning over evidence therefore acts as an arbiter of conflicting neighbors rather than as a source of knowledge, and no single-number leaderboard can see it. Fourth, accuracy obeys a law of homology availability.
2607.26397.paper_summary_zh: 酶功能預測是一種層次化、知識密集的蛋白質功能分類形式。現有的基準揭示了一個異常現象：一般的 LLM 在粗略的第一級通常表現良好，但一旦要求完整的 EC 編號，其在第二至第四級的準確率幾乎降至零，而專門的模型和工具仍然可用。我們提出了 EC-Reason-Bench，一個無需訓練的診斷評估協議，旨在回答兩個問題：為什麼一般 LLM 在 EC 編號預測上幾乎得分為零，以及在不更新任何權重的情況下，能夠恢復多少損失。我們將酶分類能力分解為四個正交的杠杆，每個杠杆都可以單獨測量：輸出結構、外部知識、推理結構和推理穩健性。我們使用推理時的方法對每個杠杆進行測試，並與共享的零-shot 基準進行比較，以重現先前報告的近零性能。對幾個強推理 LLM 的實驗得出了四個主要發現。首先，外部知識是決定性的，必須先於推理：封閉書籍的表現普遍較低，但在開放書籍的訪問下急劇上升，縮小了模型之間的差距。第二，在封閉書籍的設置中，是否使用級聯和思維鏈會有幫助或傷害，取決於模型的自我克制傾向。第三，一旦有證據可用，最佳 LLM 設置的總體得分與僅僅投票最近檢索到的鄰居的 EC 編號無法區分；這種平局是平均的產物，並隱藏了在對抗證據集上獲得的巨大增益，與在多功能酶上遭受的同樣巨大損失。因此，對證據的推理充當了相互矛盾的鄰居的仲裁者，而不是知識的來源，並且沒有任何單一數字的排行榜能夠反映這一點。第四，準確性遵循同源性可用性的法則。
